newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money trade strained, rates steady.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money trade strained, rates steady.

text.p: Croatian interbank call money rates were mostly steady on Monday amid a modest supply of kuna funds, dealers said.
Demand overshot supply by 63 million kuna, boosted by banks' mandatory reserve payments.
"There is less and less money. We made nine loans altogether, all call money, and no term loans so far," one dealer said.
She said the call money, worth 27.5 million kuna, was granted at 10.5 percent, with one loan struck at 15 percent.
"We are putting pressure on potential creditors to get some money," the dealer said.
Overnight trade at the weekend was strained as bank accounts were empty due to cash outflows for monthly pension payments.
The trade totalled 84.5 million kuna. Four banks borrowed 21.5 million to square position and the rest went for the replenishment of mandatory reserves. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
